predecessors.name: Buyid dynasty
predecessors.text: Mayyafariqin and the Diyarbakir area, taken by Badh ibn Dustak after the death of the Buyid emir Adud al-Dawla in 983

successors.name: Great Seljuk Empire
successors.text: Diyar Bakr: Mayyafariqin, Amid, Akhlat, Manzikert, Nisibis, Ercis, Muradiye, Siirt, Cizre and Hasankeyf; "Henceforth, the Diyar Bakr fell almost entirely under the direct rule of the Seljuks"

ledger.x: 983: Badh ibn Dustak, a Kurdish shepherd, seizes Mayyafariqin.
984: towns on the north shore of Lake Van.
ledger.cp: local Armenian and Arab lords of the Lake Van shore

ledger.x: 991: al-Hasan retakes fortresses from the Hamdanids.
ledger.cpn: Hamdanid dynasty (emirates of Mosul and Aleppo)

ledger.x: 1011: Nasr al-Dawla takes over Diyarbakir directly.
1031: the Byzantines under George Maniakes retake Edessa.
1032: Nasr al-Dawla's commander Bal recaptures Edessa.
1085: the Seljuks end the Marwanid dynasty.
1085: the last emir Nasir al-Dawla Mansur falls; Jazirat ibn Umar (Cizre) was his remaining city.

wars.name: Badh ibn Dustak against the Buyids and Hamdanids
wars.outcome: Badh took Mayyafariqin and Diyarbakir in 983-984; his brother Abu l-Fawaris Hasan was killed fighting the Buyids in 987-988 and Badh himself was killed in battle against the Hamdanids in 991.

wars.name: Marwanid-Byzantine struggle for Edessa
wars.outcome: Nasr al-Dawla took Edessa in 1026; Maniakes retook it in 1031, Bal recaptured it in 1032 and the Byzantines took it again in 1033.

wars.name: Seljuk conquest of Diyar Bakr
wars.outcome: Malik-Shah I, urged by the traitor Ibn Jahir, took Mayyafariqin and Diyar Bakr; the Marwanid dynasty ended with Nasir al-Dawla Mansur in 1085.

certainty.note: A hill country of fortress towns; no treaty lines on the pages.
